title: Shuttle flights with O-ring thermal distress, by joint temperature at launch, 1981–85
description: Bar chart of the share of the 24 shuttle flights before Challenger on which the booster O-rings showed thermal distress (erosion, blow-by or excessive heating), grouped by the O-ring temperature at launch. At 66°F or above: 3 of 20 flights, 15%. At 63°F or below: 4 of 4 flights, 100%. Challenger's joint was estimated at about 28°F. Data: Report of the Presidential Commission on the Space Shuttle Challenger Accident (1986), vol. 1, chapter 6, figures 6 and 7.
heading: FLIGHTS WITH O-RING DISTRESS · %
